body.statement:
Can the joint-resolvent handle be turned into a finite, explicit deterministic system that outputs \(\mathfrak B(\xi)\), the norms \(\rho_j(b;\xi)\), limiting objective values, global-selection slacks \(G_b(\xi)\), and the branch derivatives needed for conditional plug-in inference, such that, uniformly on compact subsets of \(\{0<\kappa<\kappa_{\mathrm{bal}}\}\) with \(d_{\mathrm{col}}(\xi)>0\), the certified event has probability tending to one, \(b^\star(\xi)\ne\bot\), and for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left[
 \mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\cap
 \left\{\max_{j\in\mathcal J}
 \left|\|\widehat\beta_{jn}\|_2-
 \rho_j\{b^\star(\xi);\xi\}\right|>\varepsilon\right\}
 \right]\longrightarrow0?
\]
Can the same certified-event system then compute the exact positive, zero, and negative HIR-dividend cells, every radius-saturation boundary, and the ordering relative to \(r_D\)?  Its method-\(E\) components must use the original unique same-sample entropy weights on \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\); the uniform complement-event default is not part of the entropy-balance asymptotics.  In addition, can one prove the boundary-uniform localization and interchange needed to recover, only as \(\kappa\downarrow0\) after the proportional limits,
\[
 r_T=\frac{\kappa}{4\lambda}+o(\kappa),
 \qquad
 r_E=\frac{\kappa}{8\lambda}+o(\kappa),
 \qquad
 r_D=\frac{v_\gamma\kappa}{2\lambda}+o(\kappa)?
\]
The requested result is a proportional-Gaussian analogue, for the binary benchmark-one-half logistic specialization, of the fixed-policy-dimensional result in Theorem 4 of FangRidderXie2026.  It is not an inclusion-based extension: that theorem assumes fixed rule dimension, compact covariate support, bounded rule derivatives, and a low-dimensional or sufficiently rich balancing sieve, whereas the present model has unbounded Gaussian features, \(p_n/n\to\kappa>0\), and exact balance only on the coordinates \((1,q^\top)^\top\).
body.justification: This is the unresolved proportional-Gaussian analogue needed before any deterministic HIR ranking or phase classification can be claimed.
body.gap: FangRidderXie2026 assumes fixed rule dimension, compact covariate support, bounded rule derivatives, and a low-dimensional or rich balancing sieve; there is no inclusion-based transfer to unbounded Gaussian features, positive aspect ratio, exact linear balance, and the same-sample nonconcave selector.
body.consumer: A solution would determine method rankings for expanded-feature trial targeting; the present note does not yet provide that ranking.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct and prove a finite deterministic same-sample tilt-policy resolvent with exhaustive global selection for all three nonconcave policy objectives, and establish the boundary-uniform localization needed for the proportional small-aspect constants.
obligation.obstruction: The exact equations retain two entropy tilts, all tilt-policy overlaps, and block-Jacobian own-row responses. The logistic parameterization makes the empirical policy criterion nonconcave, so stationary fixed points neither identify the lexicographically selected global norm nor exclude branch coexistence. The fixed-dimensional theorem supplies no uniformity as dimension grows.
obligation.attempted: The exact finite-sample balance and radius-KKT equations, the conic feasibility phase, radial regret reduction, fixed-dimensional global M-estimator law, exact entropy quadratic identity, and a feasible-side conditional-energy floor were derived. Convex Gaussian minimax and independent-weight surrogates were rejected because their hypotheses or estimators differ from the frozen same-sample construction.
obligation.partial_result:
Define \(\mathbb P_nf=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf_i\) and \(W_{ian}=nw_{ian}\).  On \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\), the exact finite-sample balance equations are
\[
 \mathbb P_n[\mathbf1\{A_{ni}=a\}W_{ian}]=1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P_n[\mathbf1\{A_{ni}=a\}W_{ian}q_{ni}]=\bar q_n.
\]
For any differentiable constrained policy maximizer there is \(\tau_{jn}\ge0\) such that
\[
 \mathbb P_n\!\left[q_{ni}\sigma'(q_{ni}^\top\widehat\beta_{jn})
 \{c_{j,ni}-\lambda q_{ni}^\top\widehat\beta_{jn}\}\right]
 =\tau_{jn}\widehat\beta_{jn},
 \qquad
 \tau_{jn}(\|\widehat\beta_{jn}\|_2^2-R^2)=0.
\]
The radial identity implies that deterministic selected-norm limits would give \(r_j=\lambda g(\rho_j)\) and determine the HIR sign by comparing \(\rho_T\) and \(\rho_E\).  The fixed-dimensional theorem proves the centered normal laws and strict covariance ordering, and the global entropy-energy lemma gives an explicit all-feasible-\(\kappa\) lower floor for the strong-penalty quadratic diagnostic.  None of these results closes the same-row tilt-policy Jacobian, certifies every nonconcave global maximizer, or justifies the proportional-to-small-aspect boundary interchange.
